steps.title: A fake installer
steps.caption: The user downloads a cracked-game installer from an untrusted download site. The file itself is not yet blocked; a file-reputation service later flags it in a retrospective verdict. Evidence: file reputation
steps.defender: a retrospective file-reputation flag lands in a queue that nobody has read yet.

steps.title: The stealer wakes up
steps.caption: The installer drops and starts a second, unsigned binary in %TEMP% . It runs silently in the user's own context - no UAC (user account control) prompt, no admin rights needed. Evidence: EDR binary event
steps.defender: EDR shows an unsigned binary in %TEMP% spawned by the installer.

steps.title: Collecting the harvest
steps.caption: The stealer reads the browser password store, the cookie database, saved chat-app login tokens, and wallet folders. Nothing is sent anywhere yet. Evidence: browser-store file reads
steps.defender: EDR logs the process opening browser credential-store and cookie files - a rare access pattern for a normal app.

steps.title: Files land in the attacker's channel
steps.caption: The webhook turns the POST into chat messages: log.zip plus a text file of credentials. The attacker reads them on a phone within minutes. Evidence: no telemetry (data already gone)
steps.defender: nothing at all - no alert fires, because the data is already outside. This is the blind spot of the technique.

steps.title: Abuse begins
steps.caption: The attacker replays a stolen session cookie and signs in to the victim's webmail from another country. Evidence: impossible-travel alert
steps.defender: the identity provider raises an impossible-travel sign-in alert - often the first loud signal, hours after the theft.

steps.title: SOC verdict
steps.caption: The analyst connects DNS first-seen → the process that resolved it → the %TEMP% archive and declares an info-stealer incident. The team blocks chat-API egress for workstations and starts a full credential reset. Evidence: egress policy
steps.defender: an egress policy is deployed and a password-manager rollout is scheduled.
